transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too, doctor. I guess what brings me in is that... well, I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. 

I work in a warehouse, and lately, every little thing just pulls my attention away. A beeper will go off, or I'll hear a forklift alarm, or even just see someone moving a pallet nearby, and it completely pulls me off my count. By the time I look back at what I'm doing, I realize I've put the completely wrong numbers into the inventory. It's just getting really frustrating to deal with.
When did you first start noticing these attention problems? сда

I'd say it's been going on for about a month now. It started right around the time my husband stopped working outside the home. Our usual routine changed quite a bit when that happened, and... well, that's when I really started noticing these issues at work.
Before this past month, did you have similar problems with attention or distractibility during childhood or adulthood?

No, not really. I mean... I never had trouble paying attention when I was growing up, or when I was in school. And I've always been able to focus just fine at work before all this. It really just started being a problem this past month.
Since your husband stopped working outside the home, have you been feeling down or sad most of the day?

No, I haven't really been feeling sad or down. I mean, it's been an adjustment with him being home all day, but it hasn't made me depressed or anything like that. I just feel normal in that way, not sad.
Since your husband stopped working outside the home, have you been feeling unusually worried or nervous?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, it's definitely a change having him around the house all day, but I'm not anxious or worried about it. It's really just the distraction part that's getting to me, not nerves or anything like that.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep since these attention problems began?
No, my sleep has been pretty much the same. I haven't noticed any changes there. I still sleep about the same amount I always have.
Do you have the same difficulty concentrating when you are at home or doing other activities outside of work?

No, I haven't really noticed it then. I mean, if I'm just doing chores or out running errands, my focus is fine. It's really just when I'm trying to work or do something that needs my full attention... I don't have that same trouble if I'm just going about my normal day outside of that.
Do you feel that your attention problems are a reaction to the changes that happened after your husband stopped working outside the home?

I don't think so. I mean, it's definitely an adjustment having him around more, but I don't feel like that's what's causing the issue with my focus. It just feels like two separate things happening at the same time, you know?
Have you started taking any new medication or using any new substances in the past month?
No, I haven't. I'm not taking any new medications, and... no, I haven't started using any other substances either. Everything's just the same as usual in that regard.
Have you noticed any new problems with your memory, such as forgetting recent conversations or things you were told?
No, my memory seems fine. I haven't noticed any issues with forgetting conversations or anything like that. It's really just the focus when I'm working.
Have you had a head injury in the past month?
No, I haven't hit my head or had any kind of injury like that. Everything's been normal physically.
{"intent":"Assess the functional impact of the attention problem at work","question":"How much has this difficulty affected your ability to perform your job?""}

It's definitely caused some hiccups. I've actually made a few inventory errors lately, so... I've had to start double-checking things with my supervisor just to make sure I'm getting it right. And honestly, it's spilling over at home, too. My husband and I have been arguing enough lately that it just feels like we’re... walking around each other, you know? Instead of actually settling into his retirement like we're supposed to be doing.
Do you also find yourself losing track of conversations with your husband at home because your attention drifts?

No, not really. I mean, I hear what he's saying just fine. I'm not zoning out or losing track of our conversations. The arguments are more about... well, just the tension between us, I guess. The trouble with my focus is really just happening when I'm trying to get my tasks done at work.
When you work in a quiet area without alarms or nearby activity, do you still have trouble concentrating?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. There aren't exactly any quiet areas where I work. It's a warehouse, so there's always something going on... forklifts backing up, people moving pallets, alarms beeping. So I haven't really had a chance to see if my focus is any better when it's completely quiet.
Do you have the same trouble staying focused when doing other tasks that require sustained attention, such as reading or paperwork?

I don't really do much reading or paperwork, honestly. My job is pretty hands-on, just moving things around the warehouse, and when I get home, I usually just watch TV or try to unwind. So I can't really say if I'd have trouble focusing on something like a book or forms. I just haven't really had to do anything like that lately.
When you use earplugs or work in a less noisy area, does your concentration improve?

Well, like I said, there really aren't any quiet areas in the warehouse, and I don't use earplugs because I need to be able to hear what's going on around me for safety. But that's actually the main reason I'm here. I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. I'll be doing a count, and a beeper goes off, or a forklift alarm sounds, or I just see someone moving a pallet out of the corner of my eye, and it completely pulls my attention away. By the time I look back, I've lost my place and realize I've put the wrong numbers into the inventory. It's just happening all the time now.
Since your husband stopped working outside the home, have you felt more stressed or overwhelmed than usual?

Not really, no. I mean, him being home hasn't really added to my stress or anything. We just kind of have our own routine now. So, no, I haven't noticed feeling any more overwhelmed because of that. It's really just the distraction stuff at work that's been getting to me.
Does your attention get pulled away during other tasks at work, or only when you are counting inventory?

I haven't really noticed it happening with other tasks, to be honest. Most of what I do is just physical, you know, lifting and moving boxes around. That doesn't really take much concentration. It's... it's really just when I have to stop and actually count things and get the numbers right that I realize how badly my attention is getting pulled away. So, yeah, I'd say it's pretty much just the inventory.
